Commentary.Commentary: Right then, the first T20I of this long five-match series is done and dusted and we have all witnessed a highly entertaining game. The action now moves to Seddon Park in Hamilton for the 2nd T20I which will be played on Sunday, 14 January and will begin at 11.40 am IST (6.10 am GMT). Our build-up though will begin much sooner. So, do join us then. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand says that the initial partnerships got them to that total which they were not sure would've been enough. He credits the bowlers for bowling great lines and lengths and gives a special mention to Tim Southee for his outstanding figures on such ground. He further talks about Tim Southee and credits his hard work and says he is pretty proud of the way Tim performs against tough sides like Pakistan. He then says it's great to see a fantastic crowd and good support for both teams. He concludes that there are just a few things to work on but everything seemed to go well in this game.

Pakistan's skipper Shaheen Afridi says that it is a proud moment for him to captain Pakistan. Mentions that it was not easy for the pacers due to the short boundaries but it is just the start. States that they will try to give their best in the next games. Credits Kane Williamson and Daryl Mitchell for the way they batted. Feels that the debut from Abbas Afridi and Saim Ayub's innings were the positives and adds that they need to give youngsters time ahead of the World Cup. Ends by saying that they will be playing back-to-back games and feels that they need to be more accurate with the ball.

Daryl Mitchell is the Player of the Match for his fabulous knock. He starts off saying that you never know what is a good total here and the partnership between him and Kane Williamson and then with Glenn Phillips allowed them to get to that total. He then says that everybody has plans in place and the wicket has good pace and bounce to offer although good cricketing shots will get you runs. He then concludes that he loves playing for the country and coming out in front of such great crowds.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Pakistan won the toss and opted to field first on what looked like a pristine wicket. Shaheen Afridi dismissed Devon Conway in the first over itself but then came the hammering from Finn Allen who did get out on a No Ball and mustered up quick runs before falling inside the Powerplay yet again. It was then the dynamic duo of Kane Williamson and Daryl Mitchell that came good for New Zealand once again and the latter simply smashed it to all parts of the ground. Adam Milne hit a few lusty blows and Mark Chapman's stellar cameo in the end took the Black Caps to a mammoth total of 226. For Pakistan, the debutant Abbas Afridi stood out with the ball as he took three scalps and remained fairly economical given the runs scored in the game and so did Haris Rauf. Rest of the bowlers were handed a thumping and two of them even conceded more than 50 runs in their 4 overs. Coming to the chase, the game hung in the balance for a long time but when it really mattered, the hosts got the wickets and sealed the win.

Pakistan will be kicking themselves as they were ahead of the required rate in the Powerplay and even inside the first 10 overs but they simply made a few critical errors that cost them dearly. Saim Ayub started in fantastic style but a bit too much eagerness cost him his wicket as he was run out early in the game. Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam kept up the good work but Rizwan couldn't cash in on the brilliant start. Fakhar Zaman came in and went away after a start as well and so did Iftikhar Ahmed leaving too much to do for Babar Azam. Babar did score a quick fifty but with wickets tumbling at the other end, he too couldn't hold on for much longer. After Babar's wicket, the tail just crumbled and what could have been a win turned into a huge loss instead.

What a high-scoring contest we have witnessed at Eden Park in Auckland! A shade over 400 runs were scored but in the end, it was the home side, New Zealand who were able to get those crucial wickets in the latter half of the chase and have taken the early 1-0 lead in the five-match series with a huge win. New Zealand were peppered early on by the Pakistani openers and conceded plenty of boundaries throughout the Powerplay but they were able to get a couple of wickets inside the first 6 overs. After that, the runs kept on flowing but a stunning catch off his own bowling by Ish Sodhi sent the dangerous Fakhar Zaman packing and the Kiwis were able to stem the flow of runs a bit. The pacers then made good use of the slower ball in the second half and were brilliantly led by the experienced Tim Southee who finished with 4 wickets and went past the 150 T20I wickets, the first male player to do so. Ben Sears and Adam Milne were ablso able to get wickets off those slower deliveries and the catching remained unblemished towards the end.

OUT! WHAT A CATCH! Tim Southee takes two in the over to wrap up the proceedings! Southee digs it in short, outside off, pace off again, Haris Rauf waits for the ball to arrive and tries to flat bat this one but gets it off the bottom half of the bat. Skies it high in the air towards cover-point. Mark Chapman keeps his eyes on the ball all the way through and settles under the skier. The ball swirls away a bit at the last moment but Chapman reacts well to dive to his right and takes it. New Zealand win by 46 runs and go 1-0 up in the series!

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 17.6: Tim Southee to Haris Rauf, OUT! c Mark Chapman b Tim Southee.

OUT! TAKEN! There it is, the 150th T20I wicket for Tim Southee! Another one bites the dust for Pakistan and New Zealand are closing in on a comfortable victory! Slower and shorter, outside off, Abbas Afridi backs away and tries to slap this one on the off side. No pace on the ball means that he has to generate power to clear the fence. He fails to do so and hits it only as far as deep cover. Matt Henry stationed in the deep, runs in and dives forward to complete the catch. Tim Southee gets his third wicket and New Zealand are just a wicket away from taking the lead in the series!

Commentary.Commentary: Still pretty short but the line is on off and middle, Babar Azam plays it off the back foot down to long on and rotates the strike.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Dropped short again and the line is down the leg side, Babar Azam gets down on one knee and sweeps it over short fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Ish Sodhi to Babar Azam, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it on a shorter length at just 84.3 clicks and around leg stump, the ball slides on and Fakhar Zaman hangs back before working it behind square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Ish Sodhi to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for some spin as Ish Sodhi comes on to bowl.
Finishes the over well. Pitches it on a hard length, around the corridor of off, Babar Azam stays back in the crease and knocks it to mid on for no run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Tim Southee to Babar Azam, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A fraction shorter on a length, angling away with no pace around off, Fakhar Zaman advances down the track and taps it to point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Tim Southee to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Great ball to the new batter. Pitches this on a length, just outside off with no pace. Fakhar Zaman gets deceived by the pace off and is beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Tim Southee to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The explosive Fakhar Zaman makes his way out to the centre.

OUT! TAKEN! The off-paced delivery works well for Tim Southee here. Southee runs in and digs in a short ball over the stumps but takes pace off the ball. Mohammad Rizwan comes down the pitch to slog it away leg side but is way too early in the shot. The ball holds a bit and then goes straight up off the top edge of the bat. The ball comes down near the leg gully region where the keeper, Devon Conway settles under it and takes a simple catch. Rizwan departs after a promising start.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Conway b Tim Southee
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Tim Southee to Mohammad Rizwan, OUT! c Devon Conway b Tim Southee.

Commentary.Commentary: A fraction short this time, around middle, Babar Azam stands tall and slashes it to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Tim Southee to Babar Azam, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Comes from over the wicket and pitches it on a good length, just outside off with no pace whatsoever. Babar Azam tries to poke at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Tim Southee to Babar Azam, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of ends for Tim Southee (1-0-12-0).
FOUR! Slower one but the line is all wrong. Dug in a bit short but around the hips, Mohammad Rizwan stays put and just helps it on its way wide of the man at short fine leg and picks up a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Takes pace off and bowls it shorter at the body, Babar Azam tucks it away in front of square on the leg side and gets a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Adam Milne to Babar Azam, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Pakistan are off to a real flier here. Short of a length and outside off, Babar Azam waits on the back foot and deliberately slaps it in the air and gets it well over the fielder at point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Adam Milne to Babar Azam, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Hit hard but straight to the fielder. Fuller in length and well outside off, Babar Azam latches onto the width and slaps it straight to the man at point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Adam Milne to Babar Azam, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, bowled fuller and it is the leg cutter, Rizwan pushes it out on the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! That has flown over the keeper's head for a maximum. Hits the deck hard around off and gets the ball to skid on. Mohammad Rizwan looks to have a swipe across the line but gets hurried on. The ball takes the top edge an flies over the ropes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! The attempted slower one, full and spilled down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full at the stumps, pace on this time, Mohammad Rizwan jams it down to mid on and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Matt Henry to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice change of pace from Matt Henry as he bowls it pace-off and on a nagging length around off. Mohammad Rizwan is drawn forward but ends up playing all around the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Matt Henry to Mohammad Rizwan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it full and at the stumps, angling back in, Babar Azam whips it uppishly and off the inner half of the bat in front of deep square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Matt Henry to Babar Azam, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length outside off, tapped away in front of cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Matt Henry to Babar Azam, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Banged in well short and outside off, Babar Azam looks to take on the pull but the ball comes off the top edge and flies in front of deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Matt Henry to Babar Azam, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, driven firmly but right back at the bowler who gets a good hand on it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Matt Henry to Babar Azam, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...just falls safely! Hits the deck hard and bowls it over off stump, Babar Azam looks to force the lofted shot but the length isn't full enough. The ball gets sliced away wide of mid off where Kane Williamson scampers but can't get to the ball. A single is taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Adam Milne to Babar Azam, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length outside off, Babar Azam stays back and dabs it down to the right of short third man but can't get it past the man.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Adam Milne to Babar Azam, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slightly shorter and outside off, coming on quickly, Rizwan slaps away the cut shot down to third man and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Wow, that is a shot and a half! Hard length over middle stump, Mohammad Rizwan keeps a low center of gravity and uses his wrists to whip this one right off the middle of the bat. The ball just sails well into the stands over the square leg fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Babar Azam walks in at number 3 for Pakistan.

OUT! RUN OUT! An absolute howler for Saim Ayub and Pakistan but brilliant work from Adam Milne. Milne steams in and serves it in the blockhole outside off. Mohammad Rizwan looks to drive but gets an inside edge back onto the pads and the ball rolls onto the deck. Ayub is itching to get to the other end and is already halfway down the track. Milne picks up the ball, turns and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. The replays show that even the dive couldn't save Ayub and he will be utterly disappointed.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, OUT! run out (Adam Milne).

Commentary.Commentary: Is that out? Adam Milne with a direct hit and New Zealand think they have got their man. And yes, the replays confirm that Ayub is short of his crease despite the dive.

FOUR! A classical off drive from Mohammad Rizwan and that was pleasing to the eye. Starts off with a quick and full delivery around off, Rizwan just leans on and presents the full face of the bat before driving it sweetly to the right of mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Adam Milne to Mohammad Rizwan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Adam Milne is brought into the attack.

FOUR! Ends with another boundary and 17 runs come off that over. Matt Henry changes the angle of attack by coming from around the stumps and serves it in the slot around off. Saim Ayub crouches a bit to get under it and thumps it over mid off for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Matt Henry to Saim Ayub, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! This is dug in short at the body with good pace behind it, Saim Ayub gets inside the line and hooks it using quick hands well over the fine leg fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Matt Henry to Saim Ayub, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Unlucky as that was timed really well. Full and outside off again, Saim Ayub lathers the cover drive but hits it straight to the fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Matt Henry to Saim Ayub, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! High, high and travels the distance! Matt Henry pitches this one up outside the line of off stump, Saim Ayub reaches out and gets underneath it before lofting it over the wide long off fence for a maximum.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Matt Henry to Saim Ayub, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length around off, angling back in, Mohammad Rizwan gets across the line a bit and tucks it away around the corner for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Matt Henry to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED AGAIN! This was more of a reaction catch and sometimes those stick and sometimes they don't. Matt Henry begins with a full ball, pitched up on the off stump, Mohammad Rizwan leans on and ends up chipping it to the left of the bowler. Henry sticks out a left hand but the ball hits the palm hard and falls out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Matt Henry to Mohammad Rizwan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be Matt Henry to steam in from the other end.

PUT DOWN! Would you believe it? It is the skipper Kane Williamson with one of the safest pairs of hands who has dropped a simple chance. Tim Southee bowls it on a hard length around off stump, Saim Ayub comes down the pitch and looks to force it over mid off but miscues it badly. Williamson dives forward and gets both hands on it but shells it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Tim Southee to Saim Ayub, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Wow, Saim Ayub has come out all guns blazing! Bowled back of a length and outside off, Ayub picks up the length early and gets in position before pulling it high over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Tim Southee to Saim Ayub, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes wider on the crease and angles it in on a tad fuller length onto off and middle. The ball nips away a bit and Mohammad Rizwan plays it off the inside half of the bat behind square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Tim Southee to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up again in the channel around off and shaping away from the right-hander, Mohammad Rizwan strokes it away to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Tim Southee to Mohammad Rizwan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches this one up around the off stump and shaping back in, Saim Ayub presents the full face of the bat and just pushes it back past the bowler for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Tim Southee to Saim Ayub, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Slashed away by Saim Ayub! Tim Southee starts off with a shortish ball, wide of the off stump, Ayub comes down the pitch and slaps it away over cover-point to begin proceedings with a boundary. Pakistan are up and running.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Tim Southee to Saim Ayub, Four!
